summary: Max Ryabinin, VP of Research and Development at Together AI, presents research on extending transformer context lengths to 5 million tokens. Motivation stems from agent applications needing large context windows and video generation requiring temporal consistency across many frames. Training long-context transformers faces two bottlenecks: quadratic computation from pairwise attention interactions and linear memory growth with sequence length. The talk walks through a cumulative optimization stack using a Llama 3B model targeting 3 million tokens on a single 8xH100 node. First, model parameters alone exhaust GPU memory. Fully sharded data parallelism chunks parameters across 8 GPUs but still runs out due to attention activations. DeepSpeed Ulysses context parallelism assigns one attention head per GPU, computing attention over the full sequence while communicating activations, yielding approximately 8x activation reduction and enabling use of Flash Attention. Activation checkpointing provides another 8x reduction by recomputing activations during the backward pass. CPU offloading of transformer block inputs, first implemented by Unsloth, stores activations on CPU when not needed, with minimal performance impact via prefetching during backpropagation. Chunked sequence training (Arctic sequence length training) tiles element-wise computations to avoid allocating 3-million-wide buffers. The novel contribution, Untied Ulysses, goes deeper into context parallelism. The key insight is that computing one set of heads at a time already saturates GPU compute, so multiple heads scheduled on one GPU can be divided into chunks and processed iteratively, reusing buffers across iterations instead of allocating one large buffer. This further reduces activation memory with negligible throughput impact at small scales. Results at 8B and 32B parameter scales match the most memory-optimized transformer training baselines while extending sequence length 25% beyond prior Ulysses implementations, sometimes outperforming at shorter context lengths. Chunk size trades memory for throughput. U-Pipe can be applied on top for additional memory savings across pipeline stages. The talk concludes that bottlenecks appear unexpectedly and recommends tools like PyTorch profiler for debugging.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

takeaways: A standard Llama 3B model's parameters alone exhaust GPU memory when targeting 3 million token contexts on an 8xH100 node.
The optimization stack is cumulative: FSDP, DeepSpeed Ulysses (~8x), activation checkpointing (~8x), CPU offloading, and chunked sequence training each provide incremental memory reductions.
DeepSpeed Ulysses context parallelism assigns one attention head per GPU over the full sequence, enabling Flash Attention while reducing activation memory ~8x.
Untied Ulysses is the novel contribution: it chunks attention heads further and reuses buffers across iterations, cutting activation memory with negligible throughput impact at small scales.
At 8B and 32B scale, Untied Ulysses matches the most memory-optimized baselines while extending sequence length 25% beyond prior Ulysses implementations.
Chunk size trades memory for throughput: larger chunks use more memory but run faster.
Bottlenecks appear where least expected; tools like PyTorch profiler are essential for debugging memory issues in long-context training.
U-Pipe can be applied on top of the optimization stack for additional memory savings across pipeline stages.

sections.title: Introduction and Together AI Overview
sections.summary: Max Ryabinin introduces himself as VP of R&D at Together AI, an AI native cloud providing GPU infrastructure, model customization (fine-tuning, RL), and inference services with 200+ models. The talk focuses on model training and fine-tuning.

sections.title: Motivation for Long Context Models
sections.summary: Community interest in long context training is driven by agent applications needing large context windows and video generation requiring temporal consistency across many frames. Understanding memory usage matters even at sub-million token scales for potential reinvestment of freed memory.

sections.title: Problem Statement and Goal
sections.summary: Extending transformer context faces two bottlenecks: quadratic computation from pairwise attention interactions and linear memory growth. The goal is to see how far existing and new techniques can push context length limits.

sections.title: Cumulative Optimization Stack
sections.summary: Starting with a Llama 3B model targeting 3M tokens on 8xH100, parameters alone exhaust memory. The stack proceeds through fully sharded data parallelism (parameters chunked across 8 GPUs, still OOM from attention activations), DeepSpeed Ulysses context parallelism (~8x reduction, one head per GPU), activation checkpointing (~8x more), CPU offloading of transformer block inputs (first implemented by Unsloth, ~37 GB offloaded), and Arctic chunked sequence training to tile element-wise computations. Together these enable 3M tokens.

sections.title: Untied Ulysses: Novel Contribution
sections.summary: The key insight is that one set of heads already saturates GPU compute per iteration, so multiple heads on one GPU can be chunked and processed iteratively, reusing buffers across iterations instead of allocating one large buffer. This further reduces activation memory with negligible throughput impact at small scales.

sections.title: Results and U-Pipe
sections.summary: At 8B and 32B scales, Untied Ulysses matches the most memory-optimized baselines while extending to 5M tokens (25% beyond prior Ulysses), sometimes outperforming at shorter contexts. Larger chunk size increases memory but improves speed. U-Pipe can be applied on top for additional memory savings across pipeline stages.

sections.title: Takeaway and Conclusion
sections.summary: Long-context training bottlenecks appear unexpectedly; tools like PyTorch profiler are essential. The paper and upcoming thread provide further details.

sections.title: Q&A
sections.summary: A question about QKV quantization is clarified: the discussion concerns the query, key, and value matrices of the transformer attention layer, not quantized parameters. The challenge is allocating a tensor 3 million wide along one axis, requiring multiple techniques beyond just U-Pipe.
